completionEvent.sourceRef: R6-D's pinned stream vocabulary, applied per anthropic/claude-opus-5's own evidence — a thinking block's signature arrives across signature_delta events, so the complete replayable block exists only at content_block_stop

continuationDomain.sourceRef: continuity report §4.4, BOTH halves, applied per anthropic/claude-opus-5's own evidence. Own-state acceptance: a Claude model's own thinking blocks are replayed to it unchanged, in order, with signatures intact. Why the domain is NARROW: prior thinking/redacted_thinking blocks are tied to the model that produced them, so "same provider" is not automatically "same continuation domain" — the domain is this model alone.

pricing.sourceRef: https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/about-claude/pricing (301 → https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing; both retrieved 2026-09-08) — the vendor's own Model pricing table, row "Claude Fable 5.1": "Base input tokens $10 / MTok | 5m cache writes $12.50 / MTok | 1h cache writes $20 / MTok | Cache hits and refreshes $0.25 / MTok | Output tokens $50 / MTok", with the page's own footnote "Cache hits and refreshes on Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1 are priced at 0.025x the base input price. All other models use the standard 0.1x multiplier." P7a upgrade: this row previously cited the MODELS page, which states input/output and the cache-read multiplier but no cache-write rate (P6.6 could not reach the pricing page). `cacheWritePerMTokUsd` records the 5-MINUTE write ($12.50), matching every other Anthropic row here; the 1-hour write ($20) has no field of its own and is under-reported, exactly as `ModelPricing`'s one-rate-per-direction shape requires — a disclosed schema gap, not a claim the 1h rate does not exist. Batch (-50%), fast-mode and `inference_geo: "us"` (1.1x) modifiers are likewise unrepresentable and are NOT folded into these numbers.

Why the domain is NARROW: "when changing Claude models, prior `thinking` and `redacted_thinking` blocks should be stripped because they are tied to the model that produced them. continuationDomain.sourceRef: continuity report §4.4, BOTH halves. Own-state acceptance: §4.4 requires the model's own assistant blocks — `thinking` with its signature, `redacted_thinking` — replayed unchanged and in order across a tool loop. Why the domain is NARROW: Anthropic documents model switching as a boundary at which those blocks are STRIPPED, because they are tied to the producing model; "same provider" is therefore not "same continuation domain", and this domain is the model alone.

summaryRequest.sourceRef: continuity report §6.1 — `config.thinkingConfig.includeThoughts: true` on generateContent. continuationDomain.sourceRef: continuity report §6.1, BOTH halves. Own-state acceptance: a `thoughtSignature` is returned to the SAME model on its exact original part — "do not concatenate signed parts; do not move a signature to a different part; preserve every accumulated signature in a sequential function-call turn". Why the domain is NARROW: "A Gemini summary can be forwarded to another family. The `thoughtSignature` cannot." Signatures are bound to their exact part and model, so the domain is this model alone.

readableState.sourceRef: continuity report §5.1 — `reasoning.summary` asks for readable summary content; the raw chain is never exposed

summaryRequest.sourceRef: continuity report §5.1 — "Current summary values are `auto`, `concise`, and `detailed`"; the deprecated `generate_summary` alias is deliberately NOT listed

replayScope.sourceRef: continuity report §5.3 — under `store: false` the COMPLETED output items of the current turn are replayed in their original order

completionEvent.sourceRef: WS-13 §8.2 (amended) — "OpenAI completed reasoning items (never the `output_item.added` partial) replayed in order under `store:false` + `include: ["reasoning.encrypted_content"]`"

continuationDomain.sourceRef: continuity report §5.1/§5.3 for own-state acceptance — under `store: false` with `include: ["reasoning.encrypted_content"]`, the model's own COMPLETED reasoning items are replayed to it in their original order on the next request — and §2.5/§7 for the narrowness: the opaque item stays with OpenAI, and no documentation places two OpenAI models in one domain. Winter records the MODEL ALONE rather than the provider: WS-13 §8.2 makes continuation domain a first-class fact that is never inferred, and a wider domain would license a cross-model fallback nothing has proven.
